_doc: Port policy for the upstream radar (scripts/upstream-radar.ts). veyyon ports upstream BUG FIXES, not direction: features, refactors, and docs follow veyyon's own roadmap. allowedTypes filters merged upstream PRs by conventional-commit type; titleAllowRegexes admits unprefixed titles that are clearly fixes. divergedSurfaces names the places veyyon deliberately went a different way: a fix touching one still gets filed, but its issue carries the surface's note so the port maps the underlying fix onto veyyon's design instead of importing upstream's.

divergedSurfaces.name: model catalog, IDs, types, and roles
divergedSurfaces.note: veyyon owns its own model catalog: model IDs, model types/tiers, role handling, and provider discovery all diverge from upstream. Never import upstream's model list, id scheme, or role table. Port the underlying bug (wrong limit, broken parse, bad fallback) onto veyyon's catalog structures, or declare NOT-APPLICABLE if the bug only exists in upstream's scheme.

divergedSurfaces.name: branding, install, and website
divergedSurfaces.note: veyyon's brand, install flow, docs, and website are fully its own. Port only behavior fixes that survive the rebrand; never upstream copy, naming, or visual direction.

neverPorted._doc: Paths a port PR may not author, enforced by `jules-port-manager.ts land`. A port of one upstream bug fix touches the source that holds the bug, its test, and its changelog entry, so anything listed here came from the session's environment rather than from the fix. What a stray path proves depends on its tier. `quarantine` paths are always noise: every Jules session runs an older bun that strips `configVersion` from bun.lock, and sessions leave scratch helpers at the repo root (#201 shipped 14 beside a good one-file fix). Those are reset to main's content inside the merge commit, named in the log, and the fix still lands. `owned` paths belong to main and a port has no business rewriting them, but a single hit is usually harmless drift such as the `Verified against <sha>` freshness stamp #196 refreshed in docs/internal/releasing.md, so one or two are quarantined the same way. `refuseThreshold` or more of them at once means something else entirely: the branch is a whole-tree revert, which is what a stale Jules clone produces when it resolves `merge main` in its own favour. #184/#186/#187 hit 183, 248 and 183 owned paths, and #195/#199/#200 hit 66 each. Such a diff is refused outright rather than filtered, because the same staleness that reverted the docs also reverted source files that no path list can recognise: #184 quietly reverted packages/argot and packages/catalog too. Note that crates/vendor/ is deliberately absent. veyyon carries uu-rm as vendored source, so a real fix can and does live there (#185).
